description: The product frontier induces a highly heterogeneous divisor-incidence network: integers are covered when some left-right divisor pair activates them. This card studies record gaps as a percolation or matching phenomenon on that arithmetic graph rather than as a raw sequence problem.
mathematical_formalization: For each x \le X define E_x = \{(r,c)\in R_n\times C_n : rc=x\}. Coverage of x means E_x\neq\emptyset. Aggregate the E_x into a bipartite divisor graph with degree distribution inherited from divisor counts and analyze consecutive covered blocks via branching or matching heuristics.
analogical_connections: online bipartite matching with forbidden edges
implementation_hypothesis: Construct local divisor-incidence graphs around record gaps and compare them with degree-preserving random bipartite surrogates. If T consistently lives in a supercritical coverage regime while null models do not, the arithmetic structure is doing real work.
experiment_seed: For each record gap interval, compute degree statistics of the covering witness graph and compare against shuffled and configuration-model baselines.

closest_prior_art.title: An optimal algorithm for on-line bipartite matching
Random graphs with arbitrary degree distributions and their applications
The multiplication table problem for bipartite graphs

novelty_claim: The novelty is to regard consecutive integer coverage as a heterogeneous bipartite activation problem whose edges come from divisor arithmetic, not from a random graph generator.
differentiation: This is not a standard matching problem because many integers share strongly correlated divisor neighborhoods and the active vertex sets are mex-generated.
